events.description:
Flaten Art Museum Exhibition – Michon Weeks: Mystic Topographies

For Michon Weeks, painting is a contemplative practice akin to meditation and prayer. Working in egg tempera, oil, and acrylic, Weeks paints the quiet terrain of everyday life: yards, tree lines, and utility poles. But these paintings do not describe the ordinary elements of the Minnesota landscape. They are the artist’s method for slow, sustained presence—and an invitation to the viewer to stay with something long enough for meaning to surface.

This body of work has emerged alongside a sustained creative exchange with author, scholar, and fellow St. Olaf professor Trish Zimmerman. Audio excerpts from the mystics, read and recorded by Weeks and Zimmerman, invite visitors to explore the sacred mystery of perception.
events.title: Michon Weeks: Mystic Topographies

events.description: Marking a quarter of a century since the September 11, 2001 attacks, the Flaten Art Museum highlights a print series from its collection: Thirty-Six Views of One World Trade Center by St. Olaf alumna Brenda Berkman ’73. Berkman — the sole named class plaintiff who opened the New York City Fire Department to women firefighters in 1982 — was a fire officer and first responder at the World Trade Center on 9/11, witnessing the destruction and loss that reverberated across the country.
events.title: Brenda Berkman ’73: Thirty-Six Views of One World Trade Center

events.description: The Institute for Freedom and Community welcomes David Siemers ’91, Distinguished Professor of Political Science at the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh, to Viking Theater in Buntrock Commons to kick off the Fall Speaker Series. Siemers will present Hate the Game, Not the Player: The Politics of Rumor, Innuendo, and Allegations of Crime. Calumnies are lies designed to destroy someone or something’s reputation.  They can be a very effective political tool, but the more they are effective, the more they undermine the trust needed to maintain a liberal democracy.  This talk focuses on how calumnies work, what makes them effective, and what we can do about them, if anything, in a liberal democracy. Everyone is invited to attend the lecture.

organizer.organizer: Buntrock Institute for Freedom and Community

events.title: Hate the Game, Not the Player: The Politics of Rumor, Innuendo, and Allegations of Crime

This week’s conversation will be led by visiting fall speaker David Siemers ’91. Siemers is a Distinguished Professor of Political Science at the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh. He teaches classes in political theory and American government. His research aims to examine the intersection of theories of politics with political practice. His most recent book is The Myth of Coequal Branches, and he is currently writing a book on the political lies and what to do about them. He was educated in the public schools of West Bend, Wisconsin, majored in political science at St. Olaf, and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

events.description:
Everyone is welcome to attend the Boldt Chair Keynote Speaker lecture, presented by Mariselle Meléndez, Ph.D.

From the eighteenth century onward, thinkers in Europe, Latin America, and the United States argued that literature, the arts, and the study of languages were essential to the formation of an engaged citizen. This talk traces that idea across these contexts and asks what it can offer us today. At a time when the humanities face mounting criticism and institutional cuts, the speaker will consider how they help people understand different histories, engage across cultures, and participate in public life. Drawing on personal experience alongside this historical perspective, the talk makes a case for the continuing importance of the humanities in a diverse society.

Snacks will be served!
events.title: Dr. Mariselle Meléndez, Ph.D. : Languages and the Humanities: Past and Present

events.description:
Faculty, staff, students, and the wider community are welcome to attend this faculty/guest recital featuring Soojung Hong, piano, and celebrating the new Steinway piano in Boe Memorial Chapel.

Dr. Soojung Hong has won national and international recognition as a pianist, and performs as a soloist or with ensemble throughout the Midwest and beyond. Her work highlights the music of female composers. See this dedication in her video production of Fanny Mendelssohn’s cycle “Das Jahr” (“The Year”)—supported by the Minnesota State Arts Board’s Artist Initiative Grant— among other notable projects. 

Dr. Hong is also a devoted educator, and many college campuses welcome her master class presentations and competition adjudications. Notably, she serves as Founder and Artist Director for the PianoFun Minnesota Festival, a piano professor at Normandale Community College, and a piano faculty member at MacPhail Center for Music and North Central University.   

This event is free and open to the public.
events.title: Boe Steinway Dedication Recital: Soojung Hong, piano
